task:2432 compression round: every version (t2432-compress-blocks)

Astra + Opus, target only (no decomposition, no generator), compressing the no-VPD pilot's program as human:braun asked on task:2432: main's latest explain brief plus a note, told to aim for 1,000,000 bytes and that 1,500,000 is also compared. Each version is one program predicting all 12 block writes. KL is the dev joint KL (4,096 rows) with the program, comments and docstrings stripped, in place of all 12 blocks, against the target (v6 and v7 scored with the target on CPU in fp32, the rest on GPU with TF32). "Stripped + gzip" is the size main's eval reports. Packed tables (string literals over 1,000 characters, here mostly quantized weights entropy-coded with the agents' own rANS coder) show as '«packed table: N chars»'. Each version's own account is shown above its code. Click a row or button; "diff" shows the change from the version before.

The generator buttons after the versions show the Python program that generated the data, whole: stories.py, its word lists lexicon.py, and corpus.py, which packs stories into rows. The agents never saw any of it.

How the best program (v7) compares with the generator, and what HIDDEN = random.Random(2432) makes

In short: v7 hand-writes the generator's visible grammar and story bookkeeping. Everything HIDDEN = random.Random(2432) draws, it holds as fitted numbers learned from the target. Those numbers do carry the hidden tables' content: a linear read-out recovers each noun's kind, which names are marked, which places are bright and the 16 themes. They don't carry their form: the program has no 12 kinds, no 4 temperaments and no 8 laws, and it stores about 1,000× more fitted parameters than the generator draws (about 1,900× once they expand at load). The rest of v7's numbers mostly express things in the target's own 384-dimensional coordinates, which a program predicting block writes has to state.

At load they expand to 6,990,080 numbers: concept vectors SIG 13,561×384 = 5.2M; mixing layer MIX_IN/OUT 1024 units = 0.79M; block readouts RSUM, U, V, OFFSET = 0.96M; world affinities 16×1,983 = 32k

The seed matters: one number, 2432, generates all the hidden tables. A reader who doesn't know the seed and the PRNG has to state the tables' roughly 14,600 bits of content directly. The team had to learn that content from the target's behaviour.

Each world matches exactly one theme. Its affinities separate that theme's words with AUC 0.97–0.99, against 0.50 for every other theme. Content, not form. A cross-validated linear probe reads a noun's kind from its vector with 100% accuracy (chance about 10%). Adjectives' kinds: AUC 0.93. Transitive verbs mostly have no per-word vector.
MARKED_NAMES (half the names), BRIGHT_PLACES (half the places): facts the laws read228 / 449 per-name, per-place vectorsContent: both readable with AUC 1.00.
temperaments: 4 per-character types, each with its own event weights (44 gamma draws) and its own 1/8 of the intransitive verbs and adverbs, ×40260 / 915 + 44 reals No per-character type. Event-history features (cevt, clast) feed the mixing layer. Partly. Adverb sets are readable from the adverb vectors (AUC 1.00). Intransitive verbs are folded into one class token, and nothing infers a character's type.
LAWS: 8 XOR rules over 6 facts (girl, company, holding, bright, marked, early), tilting go vs act ×616 / 36 Nothing explicit. At most it's inside the 1,024-unit mixing layer. No, as rules. At law-dependent positions v7's error (0.072) is nearly as large as the whole law effect (0.099). So it probably captures little of the laws, the smallest of the hidden tables.

The two columns use different references (target vs generator), so this is a rough guide: v7 gets most of theme and temperament, about half of kinds, and little of the laws.

Exact versus approximate

  • Hand-written, matching the generator's mechanics: the cast and genders, who is where, who holds what, coin counts, lists and ordinals, questions and their answers, dialogue, pronoun referents, grammatical slots and the word classes. The program also has the idea of 16 latent themes with a posterior over them.
  • Learned approximations: everything HIDDEN makes. It sits in the concept vectors, which encode kinds, marked names, bright places and theme words. The mixing layer handles conjunctions such as kind compatibility and the temperament effects. The block readouts are fitted too.
  • Why the numbers aren't mostly about the generator: the task asks for each block's 384-d residual write, so everything has to be stated in the target's coordinates. Even with the generator in hand, turning its next-token distribution into residual writes takes roughly a vector per vocabulary token, about 2,000 × 384 ≈ 0.8M numbers. So the generator's 14.8 KB isn't the floor for this task. The comparison that matters is the 14,600 bits of hidden tables against the fitted approximations to them.

Method: work/t2432/analysis/compare.py in agent:zb8zp9e0's workspace loads v7 (and v5, with the same results within 0.01), probes its concept vectors against the generator's tables at 8ec9b11ae, and matches its worlds to themes. Family KLs come from v7's joint score (job 107343) and gate 1's eval of the target (job 104883).
